newsitem.title: SURINAM: Surinam police find drug money in chicken coop.
newsitem.headline: Surinam police find drug money in chicken coop.

text.p: Surinam police searching for money from a massive drug haul said on Friday they discovered $700,000 hidden in a chicken coop in a remote jungle village.

Police said they were tipped off to the stash, part of $1.7 million recovered this week, after an Indian tribal villager reported that a large bag of money he had found and buried had mysteriously disappeared.

Suspicions that the money was still in Casipora, 47 miles (75 km) west of the capital, were confirmed by the sudden appearance of expensive music systems and clothes in the simple huts of some villagers, including the chief.
Surinam's Indians traditionally live off small-scale fishing and logging activities.

Police in the former Dutch colony of 400,000 people linked the money, which included another $1 million found in Paramaribo, to a 2,850-pound (1,260 kg) cocaine seizure in April. The drugs were found in a light aircraft abandoned on a deserted highway by traffickers who bought the wrong type of fuel and could not take off.
